title: Simulating Coin Flips and the Semicolon-After-for Trap
description: Draw a random double with Math.random() to count heads when randomNumber > 0.5, and spot the stray semicolon on the for loop header.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Initialize int numHeads = 0 on line 3 to count how many coin flips land on heads.
Look closely at line 5: for(int i = 0; i < 10; i++); has a semicolon right before the opening brace. The following block calls Math.random() and increments numHeads when randomNumber > 0.5.

steps.question: Because of the semicolon after i++) on line 5, how many times does the block on lines 6-11 actually run?
steps.answer: The semicolon ends the for loop with an empty body that counts i to 10 by itself. The block on lines 6-11 executes only once after the loop finishes.

steps.description: See line 6 run just once after line 5, confirming that the stray semicolon detached the block from the for loop.
